$comment: Project-scoped MCP config. Open this folder in Claude Code (or any client that reads
.mcp.json) and all three MENTOR services connect — that is the fastest way to use this
product the way a student does, with a real model choosing the tools.
MENTOR is THREE deployed applications, not one, and the split is the security boundary:
MCP-3 is the only process that ever holds a flashcard answer. Connecting all three is
what makes the loop close — MCP-1 files your role choice with MCP-3 and hands the
checkpoint spec to MCP-2, and MCP-2 files its verdict back to MCP-3, which is what
releases the card once your own tests are green.
These are the LIVE services on NitroCloud (DEPLOY.md 5b), so the server-to-server
bridges are real. Needs a network, but no API key and no account.
OFFLINE INSTEAD: after npm run build:all, swap each block for its stdio equivalent —
mentor-roster   command node, args [dist/index.js], cwd mcp-roster
mentor          command node, args [scripts/start-mcp.mjs]
mentor-profile  command node, args [dist/index.js], cwd mcp-profile
The cwd matters: @nitrostack/core resolves widget HTML from process.cwd(), so launching
an entry point from the repo root dies at startup with an error about a missing HTML
file — which reads like a broken widget build and is not. scripts/start-mcp.mjs chdirs
first, which is why MCP-2 goes through it.
Offline the peer URLs are unset, so the three cannot call each other and you carry the
artifacts between them by hand. That path is fully supported and each service says so
rather than implying your work is being kept.
See WALKTHROUGH.md for what to actually say once this is connected.
